Alice: Quick RFC follow-up: token claim granularity vs runbook handling. TL;DR we need a clear fallback for expired project-scoped API keys in ingest pipelines. Thoughts?
Ben: Agree we hit this in metrics last week, e2e pipeline had ~1200 failures for 5m. Was that the project-scoped key rotation?
Chandra: It looked like project keys rotated (short TTL) and some sidecars/thumbprint caches didn't refresh. I think two problems: token lifetime + consumer retry behaviour.
Dmitri: Proposal: default to short-lived resource/project-scoped keys for writes, but provide an automated exchange path to a read-only org-scoped token on failure. That avoids full admin keys.
Elena: How does the exchange endpoint authenticate the caller? We need to ensure it only issues org-read tokens when the service has verified identity + intent.
Dmitri: Yeah, exchange requires mTLS + service identity (svc-cert) + IAM check. Also emit an audit event: auth.exchange.{success|failure}.
Ben: Can we sketch the runbook steps so oncall has a playbook rather than ad-hoc fixes?
Alice: Rough runbook scribble: 1) Detect spike in auth.expired.count or auth.failure.project-scope. 2) Identify affected service (tag via auth.context.service). 3) If >=3 failures/min, trigger automated exchange attempt (idempotent). 4) If exchange fails, fallback to delaying writes and alert SRE + product owner. 5) Postmortem + token TTL tuning.
Chandra: Important: automated exchange must be opt-in per service to avoid privilege creep. Add a per-service flag: allow_org_exchange = true.
Dmitri: Implementation note: clients should try refresh locally first, then call /auth/v1/exchange with current token. Example exchange request: ```
POST /auth/v1/exchange
Authorization: Bearer <current-token>
{ "target_scope": "org:read" }
```
Response should be short-lived token (10m) and usage metadata.
Elena: Telemetry: emit labels: {service, project, route, exchange_attempted, exchange_result}. That way we can query for services repeatedly hitting exchange.
Ben: Ops question: who can flip allow_org_exchange? Platform team only? Or service owners?
Alice: Platform + security gate. Default off. Service owners request via infra portal, with justification & risk review.
ops-bot: FYI deploy: token-exchange v0.3 rolled to canary at 1747723360 :rocket:
Chandra: Minor edge-case: fanout writers (many downstream writers using same project key) could cause thundering exchange. Add jitter + backoff in clients.
Dmitri: Agreed — client retry: exponential backoff, max 5 attempts, introduce a small randomized jitter.
Elena: And update RBAC mapping docs: clearly show org:read vs project:write intents, examples for curl + SDK.
Alice: Next actions: 1) Dmitri & Chandra flesh exchange API + auth checks (PR by EOD). 2) Ben to add runbook steps into incidents runbook page. 3) Elena to add telemetry tags. 4) Security to add policy for allow_org_exchange requests.
Ben: :thumbsup: I'll start the runbook doc.
Dmitri: I'll open the API PR, will include sample curl and a small health endpoint for canary.
Chandra: I'll add client retry guidance into the SDK readme.
Elena: Will add telemetry and an alert dashboard for auth.exchange failures.
Alice: Thanks all — tagging @oncall for visibility once runbook is up.
ops-bot: Reminder: oncall handoff in 2h.
